proposed_english: be intent in heart / set heart upon
rationale: Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'be careful, attentive, intent of heart' (Crum 511b). Three occurrences on this page (lines 9, 16, 18), all in the heretical proposition that 'God is intent in heart concerning the molding of flesh.' The phrase is theologically pointed: it ascribes deliberate divine intention toward the archonic molding — which the Apostle then refutes.

Action-noun on Greek πλάσσειν with Lycopolitan ⲧ-ⲟⲓⲛ- prefix, parallel to ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'dissolution' in glossary. Distinct from ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ 'thing-molded' — this names the act/process of molding. Chapter-heading formula.
Lycopolitan ⲭⲓ = ϫⲓ 'take' + 3sg.m suffix + ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward.' Soteriological raising-verb paralleling ⲧⲟⲩⲱ in glossary.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ + 3sg.m suffix. Standard verb of cosmic casting/throwing, here the eschatological hurling of Error down to the Deep.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' (cf. ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'the gatherer' in glossary) with object suffix. Used cosmologically of the gathering of dark substance prior to its casting-down.
Directional ⲁ- + possessive ⲧⲉϩ- 'his' + ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become, exist.' Action-noun: 'his becoming/coming-into-being.' Refers to the formation of humanity (Adam-Eve) as object of the alleged divine intent.
Obscure form functioning as topic-introducer before ⲡⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ 'the Ambassador.' Possibly Lycopolitan compound preposition. Confidence low — flagged for parallels.

Tentatively read as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄ 'examine, scrutinize, observe' — the Apostle's command to his disciples to examine the archons rather than infer divine intention. Confidence moderate.
Tentative; contextually fits a verb of expulsion in the soteriological-purpose clause. Possibly compound on ⲥⲁϩⲣ 'drive away' (cf. ⲥⲁⲍⲣⲉ in glossary). Confidence low.
